newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds close higher.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed higher in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.38/2.33 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.55/2.50 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.46/2.41 percent against 2.60/2.55 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.98/98.03 from Tuesday's close of S$97.79/97.84, September 2001 at S$96.82/96.87 versus S$96.58/96.63 and June 2003 at S$94.84/94.89 against S$94.58/94.63.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 2-15/16 2-13/16 percent from Tuesday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
